doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Staying in Rome and best and worst gigs
title: The worst gig: a solo Christmas party in Utica
summary: A solo piano job booked by Tony Cee where the crowd wanted a band, and a heckler. He notes he now plays with a smaller core of people.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: What about your worst gig ever?

Probably the worst gig in my recent history was a Christmas party that Tony Cee booked me for. It was a solo piano gig at the Radisson or at the Sheraton in Utica, an office Christmas party. And they had a piano, a little upright piano or something there. And I was very thorough when he was calling me for the gig, “are you sure they want just piano music? They’re not looking for a band? They’re not looking for a singer?” “No, no, no, they just want some Christmas tunes, nice background music, and that’s it.” “You’re positive?” “Yes, of course.” And I show up and of course they wanted Atlas Linen Company, you know, or one of those bands. And that was a difficult one. And I had one girl there who just harassed me all night. “You suck.” And by the end of the night I was going “You suck.” So yeah, that was a tough one. You’re by yourself on a little piano and what am I going to do. “Play some Elvis!” “Elvis? Okay.”
“Blue Christmas.” And you look at your watch and it’s going backwards. This gig will never end.

Yeah. It’s in reverse. Exactly. So but generally, lately, you know these days the gigs are not that bad. But I find I play with less and less people — the people I actually play with. It’s come down to like a little core. It used to be I had gigs with everyone, when I was young especially. You know, you play with everybody in the area. Now it’s just not that many. Not that many people want to play with me probably.
